card.profile: Pogonishte is a folk dance from Pogon in southern Albania. It is related to the Greek dance Pogonisios (Greek: Πωγωνίσιος) or Sta Dyo (Greek: Στα Δύο). The time signature is in 24, and it is danced in an open circle; dancers bounce twice gently on every count.
card.insight: Pogonishte is a folk dance from Pogon in southern Albania.

what_works: Dividing the song and dance into clear structural parts A, B, and C

observation.setting: A bright dance studio with a wooden floor and white walls, during a dance class or workshop.
observation.dancers: A mixed group of about 10-12 adults (both men and women of various ages).
observation.formation_and_space: A single open circle formation, holding hands and moving sideways in a line along the circumference.
observation.posture: Upright torso, relaxed posture with slight knee flexion as they step.
observation.footwork: Side-steps along the circle, crossing steps, and occasional lifts or taps, moving continuously on the beat.
observation.arms_and_hands: Hands joined in a W-position (elbows bent, hands roughly at shoulder height), swaying or moving slightly with the steps.
observation.hips_and_torso: Minimal torso movement, maintaining upright posture with gentle side-to-side travel.
observation.partnering: None; held in a circle by hand-holds.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: No major jumps or turns; performed at standing level with occasional slight lifts of the knees.
observation.costume_and_props: Casual everyday clothing (t-shirts, trousers, skirts, casual dresses).
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement on fast steps is obscured by low-resolution video and distance.

signature_moments.what: The circle moves fluidly sideways with a grapevine-like stepping pattern while holding hands in a W-position.
